site.name: Navish Kumar
site.statement: I build learning systems where mathematical structure and empirical behavior must agree before decisions are made.
site.context: This is a portfolio of one method expressed across multiple domains.

overview.scroll_note: Read this page as one argument: identity, method, questions, programs, evidence, progression.

signature.title: Formalize Early
signature.text: I start by making invariants and failure modes explicit.

signature.title: Instrument Deeply
signature.text: I build pipelines that reveal behavior, not only outcomes.

signature.title: Optimize For Consequence
signature.text: I value methods by their effect on design and operations.

overview.hero_title: I work on machine learning systems that remain reliable under real constraints.
overview.hero_subtitle: My research combines mathematical structure, system-level experimentation, and decision relevance.
overview.hero_context: Across variational inference, graph methods, and urban operations, I use one discipline: formalize assumptions, expose behavior, and optimize for consequence.
overview.identity_line: I am a theory-minded builder: I care about guarantees that survive deployment reality.
questions: Which structural assumptions make learning updates stable, interpretable, and trustworthy?
How should experimental systems be designed so evidence remains meaningful outside benchmark settings?
Where can formal guarantees be coupled with operational constraints to improve real decisions?
overview.closing_invite: The archive maps each paper to its governing question, method choice, and practical implication.
overview.method_thesis: Performance is not enough. A method is complete when its assumptions, behavior, and downstream decisions align.

frames.title: How I Think
frames.text: I begin with invariants and failure modes, then formalize what must remain true as complexity increases.

frames.title: How I Build
frames.text: I translate abstractions into datasets, optimization routines, and evaluation pipelines that expose actual behavior.

frames.title: How I Connect Theory to Practice
frames.text: I treat formal results as decision tools. A method is complete when it changes system design or operation.

logic.title: Question
logic.text: Specify the structural claim and the failure mode.

logic.title: System
logic.text: Build data and optimization pipelines where the claim can be tested.

logic.title: Decision
logic.text: Convert results into constraints, policy, or deployment guidance.

arcs.name: Mathematical Structure for Reliable Learning
arcs.thesis: Use spectral and geometric structure to explain and guarantee learning behavior.
arcs.methods: Spectral graph analysis, variational optimization, convergence proofs
arcs.practice: Improves trust in learning updates when optimization instability carries real cost.

arcs.name: Data-Driven Urban Logistics
arcs.thesis: Model city context at micro-region level so sustainability transitions become operationally testable.
arcs.methods: H3 spatial indexing, OpenStreetMap feature aggregation, predictive service-time models
arcs.practice: Supports concrete fleet and routing decisions for low-emission delivery systems.

arcs.name: Social Interaction and Counterspeech
arcs.thesis: Measure how harmful and protective speech behaviors co-evolve in online communities.
arcs.methods: Dataset construction, linguistic analysis, behavioral interaction study
arcs.practice: Informs interventions that reduce harm without relying only on blunt account removal.

timeline.title: Interaction dynamics between hate and counter users
timeline.note: Built an annotated paired-account dataset and established empirical asymmetries in behavior and strategy.

timeline.title: Normalized Laplacians for gain graphs
timeline.note: Shifted toward structural analysis by defining normalized operators and studying their spectral implications.

timeline.title: Extremal eigenvalue bounds for gain Laplacians
timeline.note: Extended the spectral program with explicit bounds linked to graph frustration measures.

timeline.title: Urban micro-region delivery performance modeling
timeline.note: Applied system modeling to practical sustainability decisions in last-mile logistics.

timeline.title: Optimization guarantees for natural-gradient variational inference
timeline.note: Unified practical optimization behavior with formal guarantees via square-root covariance geometry.

08ZZubdj9fEC.summary: Provides convergence guarantees for natural-gradient variational Gaussian inference using square-root covariance parameterization.
08ZZubdj9fEC.contribution: Closes a key theory-practice gap for methods known to perform strongly in empirical settings.
08ZZubdj9fEC.build: Derives guarantees for both discrete updates and continuous-time flow, then compares optimization geometries empirically.
08ZZubdj9fEC.impact: Supports more reliable inference pipelines where unstable updates are expensive.
08ZZubdj9fEC.timeline_note: Made natural-gradient behavior formally tractable without losing practical relevance.

738O_yMBCRsC.summary: Models delivery performance by urban micro-region to estimate where cargo-bike fleets can replace vans.
738O_yMBCRsC.contribution: Turns a sustainability ambition into a measurable operational question with replicable data abstractions.
738O_yMBCRsC.build: Combines Uber H3 partitioning with OpenStreetMap features to predict service-time components by neighborhood.
738O_yMBCRsC.impact: Provides evidence for fleet-transition and routing decisions in real city operations.
738O_yMBCRsC.timeline_note: Connected machine learning modeling to operational decision-making in urban systems.

WbkHhVStYXYC.summary: Derives lower and upper bounds for extremal eigenvalues of gain Laplacian matrices.
WbkHhVStYXYC.contribution: Extends spectral guarantees beyond signed graphs and links structure imbalance to stability-relevant eigenvalues.
WbkHhVStYXYC.build: Relates frustration number and frustration index to explicit spectral bounds through constructive proofs.
WbkHhVStYXYC.impact: Strengthens analytical tools for structured networks used in learning and control contexts.
WbkHhVStYXYC.timeline_note: Converted structural intuition in gain graphs into concrete spectral guarantees.

OU6Ihb5iCvQC.summary: Introduces normalized Laplacians for gain graphs and studies balance, bipartiteness, and spectrum relationships.
OU6Ihb5iCvQC.contribution: Builds the operator-level foundations required for later extremal eigenvalue analysis.
OU6Ihb5iCvQC.build: Defines normalized operators, proves bounds, and extends interlacing concepts in gain-graph settings.
OU6Ihb5iCvQC.impact: Provides reusable formal tools for future structured graph-learning analysis.
OU6Ihb5iCvQC.timeline_note: Established the formal baseline for subsequent gain-Laplacian results.

SP6oXDckpogC.summary: Analyzes dynamics between hate and counterspeech users on Twitter using a released paired-user dataset.
SP6oXDckpogC.contribution: Shows behavioral and linguistic asymmetries, and how counterspeech strategies differ by community context.
SP6oXDckpogC.build: Constructs and releases annotated user-pair data, then applies lexical and psycholinguistic analyses.
SP6oXDckpogC.impact: Supports moderation and intervention designs that balance harm reduction and free-expression concerns.
SP6oXDckpogC.timeline_note: Grounded early work in measurable social dynamics with immediate policy relevance.
